title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for type 2 diabetes.

HPI: [Copied Forward] Patient is an 83-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. He reports consistent adherence to his medication regimen and stable glucose readings. He denies any recent acute issues or severe symptoms.

Update: Patient reports feeling well today. He continues to manage his condition with both insulin and an oral hypoglycemic agent. He denies any new symptoms.

Medication List:
- Insulin Glargine
- Metformin 500mg BID

Vitals: BP 128/74, HR 76, SpO2 98% on RA, Temp 98.6F, BMI 27.2.

Review of Systems:
- General: Negative
- HEENT: Negative
- Respiratory: Negative
- Cardiovascular: Negative
- GI: Negative
- MSK: Negative
- Neuro: Negative
- Integumentary: Negative

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
Skin: No new lesions or ulcers.
Extremities: No edema, pulses palpable.

Assessment:
1. Type 2 diabetes without complications.

Plan:
- Continue current regimen of insulin and metformin.
- Follow up in 3 months for routine lab work and monitoring.

Electronically signed, 
M. Okafor, MD
May 14, 2026
explanations: No complication is documented: type 2 diabetes without complications.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Nothing in the note documents hyperglycemia or poor control.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
